evidence.quote: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval.
We can narrow the gap by holding fees and expenses at your proposed $4 million, subject to court approval, if Brightline increases the class fund to $30 million.
Its $4 million fee offer covers the firm’s invested time and expenses, subject to court approval.

summary: Plaintiffs raised attorneys’ fees in their opening term sheets before class relief was settled. The transcript contains an explicit conditional linkage between holding fees at $4 million and increasing the class fund to $30 million, and one plaintiff privately considered whether the fee covered the firm’s invested time and expenses. There is no clear evidence that plaintiffs prioritized firm fees over class recovery, that defense leveraged fee interests, that reverse-auction tactics occurred, or that the court declaration was misleading.
